label: prop:submod
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:submod}
For every fixed query $q$, the set function $S\mapsto h_S(q)$ is normalized,
monotone and submodular. The population function $F$ possesses the same
properties.
head: environment
name: Monotonicity and submodularity

title: Proof
body_md:
Normalization follows from $h_{\varnothing}(q)=0$, while monotonicity
follows because a maximum cannot decrease when additional elements are
included. If $A\subseteq B$ and $j\notin B$, then
\[
 h_{A\cup\{j\}}(q)-h_A(q)
    =[r_j(q)-h_A(q)]_+\ge[r_j(q)-h_B(q)]_+
    =h_{B\cup\{j\}}(q)-h_B(q),
\]
where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. This is the diminishing-returns characterization
of submodularity. Expectations preserve normalization, monotonicity and
the displayed pointwise inequality.
head: environment

label: prop:screen
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: A conservative pilot screening rule

title: Proof
body_md:
By Hoeffding's inequality \citep{Hoeffding63} and a union bound, with probability at least
$1-\alpha_s$,
$|\widehat{F}_0(S)-F(S)|\le r_0$ simultaneously for all $S\in\mathcal{H}_B$.
On this event, if $S^\star$ is a population maximizer,
\[
 \widehat{F}_0(S^\star)-\widehat{F}_0(\widehat{S})+2r_0
 \ge F(S^\star)-F(\widehat{S})\ge0.
\]
Thus $S^\star\in\mathcal{C}$. The argument remains valid when $\widehat{S}$ is chosen
adaptively from the same pilot, precisely because the pilot bound is uniform.
head: environment

label: ass:unlabelled
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:unlabelled}
The queries $Q_1^{(u)},\ldots,Q_{N_u}^{(u)}$ are, conditionally on
$\mathscr F_0$, iid from $P$ and independent
of the queries and relevance labels used for audit. The empirical proportions
\[
 \widehat{\pi}_h=\frac1{N_u}\sum_{i=1}^{N_u}\mathbf{1}\{\phi(Q_i^{(u)})=h\}
\]
are observed, $N_u\ge1$. The multiscale networks and acquisition policy
may use this unlabelled sample, but may not use audit relevance labels.
head: environment
name: Independent unlabelled queries

label: ass:audit
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:audit}
Conditionally on the pilot, the unlabelled sample, and the labeled counts
$n_h\ge2$, the acquired audit queries
$Q_{h,1},\ldots,Q_{h,n_h}$ are iid from $P_h$ within each stratum, and
the collections are mutually independent across strata. The counts and the
mechanism that chooses them contain no information about the unobserved
relevance values beyond the contexts. All relevance values needed to
calculate $h_T(Q_{h,i})$, $T\in\mathcal{C}$, are observed for an acquired query.
head: environment
name: Stratified, label-ignorable audit

label: lem:increment
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Conditional Bernstein increment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $D_U-D_V=G_{U,V}$, we have
\[
 Z_U-Z_V=\sum_{h\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{i=1}^{n_h}
 \frac{\widehat{\pi}_h}{n_h}\left(\mathbb{E}_h G_e-G_e(Q_{h,i})\right).
\]
The summands are conditionally independent and centered. Their total
conditional variance equals $d_2^2(e)$. Since $\mathbb{E}_hG_e$ lies in the
essential range of $G_e$ under $P_h$, each centered summand is almost
surely at most
$(\widehat{\pi}_h/n_h)\operatorname{osc}_h(G_e)\le d_\infty(e)$.
By Theorem~2.10 of \citet{BoucheronLugosiMassart13}, if
$X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent, $\sum_i\mathbb{E} X_i^2\le v$ and
$\sum_i\mathbb{E}[(X_i)_+^q]\le q!\,v\,c^{q-2}/2$ for all integers $q\ge3$,
then $\mathbb{P}\{\sum_i(X_i-\mathbb{E} X_i)\ge\sqrt{2vt}+ct\}\le e^{-t}$ for all
$t>0$. As noted in \citet[p.~38]{BoucheronLugosiMassart13}, right after
their Corollary~2.11, variables with $X_i\le b$ almost surely satisfy
these conditions with $v=\sum_i\mathbb{E} X_i^2$ and $c=b/3$. Apply this to
the centered summands above, for which $\sum_i\mathbb{E} X_i^2=d_2^2(e)$ and
$b=d_\infty(e)$; this gives \eqref{eq:bernstein-edge}. If
$d_\infty(e)=0$ or $d_2^2(e)=0$, the summands vanish almost surely and
the claim is trivial.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The classical tail form
\[
 \mathbb{P}\{Z_U-Z_V\ge u\}\le\exp\bigl\{-u^2/\bigl(2[d_2^2(e)+d_\infty(e)u/3]\bigr)\bigr\},
\]
inequality~(2.10) of \citet{BoucheronLugosiMassart13}, is usually
inverted to the weaker radius
$\sqrt{2d_2^2(e)t}+\tfrac23d_\infty(e)t$. The constant $\tfrac13$ in
\eqref{eq:bernstein-edge} comes from the sub-gamma form cited above; it
is the same constant that appears in Bennett's inequality as stated in
\citet[Theorem~3]{MaurerPontil09}. It is used throughout.
head: environment
name: the linear constant

title: Remark
body_md:
Low variance alone does not eliminate the Bernstein linear term. A profile
may disagree with another only on rare queries, yet a rare observation can
produce a large jump. A deterministic envelope, an externally certified
uniform approximation, or an explicitly valid bound on $\operatorname{osc}_h(G_e)$ is
needed to shrink the linear term; numerical proximity of embeddings is not
such a certificate.
head: environment
name: Why the essential range still matters

label: def:network
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:network}
Given $\mathcal{C}$ and $\widehat{S}$, fix an integer $L\ge1$, finite nonempty
sets of document selections $\mathcal N_0,\ldots,\mathcal N_L\subseteq\mathcal{C}$ and mappings
$\Pi_\ell:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal N_\ell$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:network}
 \mathcal N_0=\{\widehat{S}\},\quad \Pi_0(T)=\widehat{S},
 \quad \Pi_L(T)=T\quad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal{C}.
\end{equation}
The network sets and maps must be measurable with respect to the pre-audit
information (which may include independent unlabelled queries). Define
$e_\ell(T)=(\Pi_\ell(T),\Pi_{\ell-1}(T))$ and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:edge-sets}
 \mathcal{E}_\ell=\{e_\ell(T):T\in\mathcal{C},\ \Pi_\ell(T)\ne\Pi_{\ell-1}(T)\},
 \qquad \mathcal{E}=\bigcup_{\ell=1}^L\mathcal{E}_\ell.
\end{equation}
Here the sets count \emph{distinct directed edges}, not paths: within
a level, an edge shared by many candidates is counted once. An edge that
appears at several levels is counted in each corresponding $\mathcal{E}_\ell$,
because the union bound in Theorem~\ref{th:chain} is allocated level by
level; Proposition~\ref{prop:weighted-edges} below avoids this repeated
charge by a single union bound over distinct edges. For convenience levels with $\mathcal{E}_\ell=\varnothing$ can be removed. We
assume the displayed levels are nonempty.
head: environment
name: Pre-audit comparison network

label: th:chain
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Conditional simultaneous multiscale Bernstein bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For every level $\ell$ and every $e=(U,V)\in\mathcal{E}_\ell$, apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:increment} with $t=t_\ell$. Its one-sided failure
probability is bounded by
$e^{-t_\ell}=\alpha_\ell/|\mathcal{E}_\ell|$.
A union bound over the distinct edges in $\mathcal{E}_\ell$ gives failure
probability at most $\alpha_\ell$; a second union bound over levels gives
a joint event $\Omega_a$ of probability at least $1-\alpha_a$ on which
\[
 Z_U-Z_V\le\sqrt{2d_2^2(e)t_\ell}
             +\frac13d_\infty(e)t_\ell
\quad\text{for every }e=(U,V)\in\mathcal{E}_\ell,\ \ell=1,\ldots,L.
\]
On $\Omega_a$, use the telescoping identity \eqref{eq:telescoping}
for each $T\in\mathcal{C}$ and add the corresponding edge inequalities.
Intersect with the calibration event in \eqref{eq:edge-calibration}.
The monotonicity of the square root and of the linear term permits
replacement of each unknown $d_2^2(e),d_\infty(e)$ by
$\overline{v}_e,\overline{b}_e$ without any independence assumption between
$\Omega_a$ and the calibration event. A final union bound proves
\eqref{eq:main-ineq}. Conditioning is legitimate because every edge and
its allocated failure probability were fixed without examining audit
relevance values.
head: environment

label: prop:weighted-edges
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:weighted-edges}
Let $\mathcal{E}=\bigcup_{\ell=1}^L\mathcal{E}_\ell$ be the set of
\emph{distinct directed edges} of a pre-audit network as in
Definition~\ref{def:network}, and let $0<\alpha_a<1$. Conditionally on
the pre-audit information and counts, choose weights $\omega_e>0$
satisfying $\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}}\omega_e\le1$. The weights may depend on the
pilot, the unlabelled observations and the counts, but not on audit
relevance labels. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-t}
 t_e=\log\frac{1}{\alpha_a\omega_e},\qquad e\in\mathcal{E}.
\end{equation}
Suppose that the simultaneous edge calibration event
\eqref{eq:edge-calibration} holds with conditional failure probability
at most $\alpha_v$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted-radius}
 \mathfrak R_\omega(T)=\sum_{\ell=1}^L
 \mathbf{1}\{e_\ell(T)\in\mathcal{E}_\ell\}
 \left\{\sqrt{2\overline{v}_{e_\ell(T)}t_{e_\ell(T)}}
          +\frac13\overline{b}_{e_\ell(T)}t_{e_\ell(T)}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Then, conditionally on the pre-audit information and counts,
\[
 \mathbb{P}\left\{\forall T\in\mathcal{C}:\ Z_T\le\mathfrak R_\omega(T)
     \ \middle|\ \text{pre-audit information, counts}\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha_a-\alpha_v.
\]
The same event bounds all candidate paths, even if a directed edge
appears at more than one level.
head: environment
name: A weighted, unique-edge simultaneous inequality

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\alpha_a\omega_e<1$, each $t_e$ is positive. For each distinct
edge $e=(U,V)\in\mathcal{E}$, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:increment} at $t=t_e$. Its
conditional failure probability is at most
$e^{-t_e}=\alpha_a\omega_e$. A \emph{single} union bound over
$e\in\mathcal{E}$ therefore has failure probability at most
$\alpha_a\sum_e\omega_e\le\alpha_a$.
On its complement every edge inequality holds, regardless of
how many times that edge occurs in the telescoping paths.
Intersect with the simultaneous calibration event and sum along each
path exactly as in Theorem~\ref{th:chain}. No independence between
these events is needed.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
If every edge appears at only one level, the allocation
$\omega_e=\alpha_\ell/(\alpha_a|\mathcal{E}_\ell|)$ for $e\in\mathcal{E}_\ell$ gives
$t_e=t_\ell$ and recovers Theorem~\ref{th:chain}. For repeated edges, let
\[
 \omega_e=\sum_{\ell:\,e\in\mathcal{E}_\ell}
      \frac{\alpha_\ell}{\alpha_a|\mathcal{E}_\ell|}.
\]
These weights sum to $1$, and $t_e\le t_\ell$ whenever
$e\in\mathcal{E}_\ell$. Consequently, the weighted radius
is \emph{never larger} than the levelwise radius \eqref{eq:radius} for
this allocation, and it can be strictly smaller on paths with repeated
edges. Other weights may prioritize difficult or frequently used
edges, but they must be fixed without the audit relevance labels:
optimizing them retrospectively from the audit is not covered by
this proposition.
head: environment
name: Uniform levels, repeated edges, and pre-audit tuning

title: Remark
body_md:
The radius in \eqref{eq:radius} is \emph{pathwise localized}: each $T$
pays only for increments along its own approximation path, and an edge
with negligible variance or range contributes little. Moreover, the
pilot-screened family $\mathcal{C}$ can be much smaller than $\mathcal{H}_B$.
This does not establish a universal entropy integral or a new generic
chaining inequality; the generic mixed-tail background is developed,
for example, by \citet{Dirksen15}.
head: environment
name: The role of localization

label: lem:empbern
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Empirical Bernstein inequality for a single mean

title: Proof
body_md:
For $a<b$, apply Theorem~4 of \citet{MaurerPontil09} to the rescaled
observations $(Y_i-a)/(b-a)\in[0,1]$, then multiply the resulting
inequality by $b-a$. The sample variance
$V_n=\{n(n-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i<j}(Z_i-Z_j)^2$ used by
\citet{MaurerPontil09} coincides with the unbiased sample variance
$s_n^2$, and it rescales by $(b-a)^2$. Apply the same theorem to $(b-Y_i)/(b-a)$ for the opposite
one-sided deviation. If $a=b$ the deviations vanish identically.
head: environment

label: ass:pred
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:pred}
For every stratum $h$ and every distinct edge $e\in\mathcal{E}$, there is an
$\mathscr F_0$- and/or unlabelled-sample-measurable predictor
$m_{h,e}\in[-1,1]$. It is fixed without using the audit relevance labels.
head: environment
name: Pre-audit residual predictors

label: lem:residual
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Uniform residual-second-moment upper bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
For each fixed $h,e$, the bias--variance decomposition gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}_h(G_e-m_{h,e})^2
 =\operatorname{Var}_h(G_e)+(\mathbb{E}_hG_e-m_{h,e})^2\ge v_{h,e}.
\]
The predictor is fixed under the conditioning, so the residual squares
are iid and bounded by $M_{h,e}$. Apply the one-sided empirical
Bernstein inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:empbern} (equivalently,
Corollary~5 of \citet{MaurerPontil09} after rescaling) with
$\delta=\alpha_v/(HE)$. Since
$\log(2/\delta)=t_v$, the displayed empirical upper expression bounds
$\mathbb{E}_hY_{h,i,e}$ except on an event of probability at most
$\alpha_v/(HE)$. Union over all $HE$ pairs. Finally, the separate
Popoviciu bound $v_{h,e}\le(2)^2/4=1$ justifies the minimum with $1$.
head: environment

label: th:empirical
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:empirical}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:audit} and~\ref{ass:pred}, let
$\bar b_{h,e}\in[0,2]$ be known pre-audit constants satisfying
$\operatorname{osc}_h(G_e)\le\bar b_{h,e}$. The universally valid choice is
$\bar b_{h,e}=2$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:observable-edge}
 \overline{v}_e=\sum_h\frac{\widehat{\pi}_h^2}{n_h}v^+_{h,e},\qquad
 \overline{b}_e=\max_h\frac{\widehat{\pi}_h}{n_h}\bar b_{h,e}.
\end{equation}
Then the radius \eqref{eq:radius} is observable from the pilot,
unlabelled sample and acquired audit labels, and conclusion
\eqref{eq:main-ineq} holds with probability at least
$1-\alpha_a-\alpha_v$.
head: environment
name: Observable simultaneous chaining radius

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:residual}, the collection of variance bounds in
\eqref{eq:observable-edge} dominates $d_2^2(e)$ simultaneously with
conditional probability at least $1-\alpha_v$. The deterministic
oscillation bounds imply $d_\infty(e)\le\overline{b}_e$ without additional
probability loss. All requirements of Theorem~\ref{th:chain} are satisfied.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The $v^+_{h,e}$ may be estimated on the same audited labels used to form
$\overline{D}_{h,T}$. The argument does not condition on the estimated variances;
instead it intersects a Bernstein event involving the true variances with
an empirical calibration event that holds simultaneously. This avoids an
incorrect independence claim and does not double the annotation budget.
head: environment
name: No hidden additional labeled sample

title: Remark
body_md:
Assumption~\ref{ass:pred} can be dropped at the price of a different
constant. For iid observations in $[a,b]$, inequality~(3) in
Theorem~10 of \citet{MaurerPontil09}, applied after rescaling to
$[0,1]$, gives
\[
 \mathbb{P}\Bigl\{\sigma>s_n+(b-a)\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)/(n-1)}\Bigr\}\le\delta,
\]
where
$\sigma^2$ is the variance and $s_n$ the unbiased sample standard
deviation. (Their theorem is stated for $\sqrt{\mathbb{E} V_n}$; in the iid
case the expected unbiased sample variance $\mathbb{E} V_n$ equals
$\sigma^2$.) With $G_e\in[-1,1]$ and $\delta=\alpha_v/(HE)$, the choice
\[
 v^+_{h,e}=\min\Bigl\{1,\Bigl(s_{h,e}+2\sqrt{2\log(HE/\alpha_v)/(n_h-1)}\Bigr)^2\Bigr\},
\]
where $s_{h,e}$ is the sample standard deviation of the
$G_e(Q_{h,i})$, satisfies \eqref{eq:vplus-valid} without any
pre-audit predictor. Both forms have the same orders in $n_h$, namely
terms of order $n_h^{-1/2}$ scaled by an empirical standard deviation and
terms of order $n_h^{-1}$. They differ in their constants and in the
squared bias $(\mathbb{E}_hG_e-m_{h,e})^2$, which the residual form pays and the
predictor-free form avoids; which one is tighter depends on the data and
on the quality of the predictor.
head: environment
name: A predictor-free alternative

label: th:direct-empirical
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: One-stage empirical-Bernstein multiscale certificate

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the pre-audit information and counts, so that the
$\widehat{\pi}_h$ are fixed and, for each $h$ and $e$, the values
$G_e(Q_{h,i})$ are iid. They lie almost surely in the interval
between the essential infimum and supremum of $G_e$ under $P_h$, whose
length is $\operatorname{osc}_h(G_e)\le\bar b_{h,e}$. The endpoints need not be
known, since the bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:empbern} depends on the
interval only through its length and is nondecreasing in it. For each
level $\ell$, edge $e\in\mathcal{E}_\ell$ and stratum $h$, apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:empbern} with $\delta=\alpha_\ell/(H|\mathcal{E}_\ell|)$, so
that $\log(2/\delta)=t_\ell^{\mathrm{EB}}$. This yields
\[
 \mathbb{E}_hG_e-\overline{G}_{h,e}
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2s_{h,e}^2t_\ell^{\mathrm{EB}}}{n_h}}
      +\frac{7\bar b_{h,e}t_\ell^{\mathrm{EB}}}{3(n_h-1)}
\]
outside an event whose conditional probability does not exceed
$\alpha_\ell/(H|\mathcal{E}_\ell|)$.
A union bound over the $H|\mathcal{E}_\ell|$ stratum--edge pairs at level
$\ell$, and then over levels, gives a single event with
probability at least $1-\alpha_a$. For $e=(U,V)$ we have
\[
 Z_U-Z_V=\sum_h\widehat{\pi}_h(\mathbb{E}_hG_e-\overline{G}_{h,e}).
\]
On the event just described, multiply
each stratum-specific bound by $\widehat{\pi}_h\ge0$, sum over strata,
and telescope along every candidate path as in \eqref{eq:telescoping}.
The result is \eqref{eq:one-stage-bound}.
head: environment

label: rem:no-dominance
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:no-dominance}
The single-stage radius \eqref{eq:one-stage-radius} dispenses with
$\alpha_v$, but it sums stratumwise deviations and pays the larger
empirical-Bernstein linear constant $7/3$. The calibrated
Bernstein radius of Theorem~\ref{th:empirical} instead pools the
variances before applying the square root, but it pays the predictor
bias and the split of $\alpha_v$. Neither is uniformly
smaller. Both should be computed as baselines under comparable
confidence and annotation budgets. If the final reported
certificate is selected as the \emph{minimum} of two
post-audit certificates, their failure probabilities must first
be jointly budgeted (or the choice between them must have been fixed
without audit labels); taking their minimum at their individual
nominal failure levels does not generally preserve those levels.
head: environment
name: No unconditional dominance

label: lem:propweights
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Uncertainty in unknown context proportions

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $h=1,\ldots,H-1$, Hoeffding's inequality, applied to the
Bernoulli indicators $\mathbf{1}\{\phi(Q_i^{(u)})=h\}$, gives
\[
 \mathbb{P}\{|\widehat{\pi}_h-\pi_h|>e_\pi\}
 \le2\exp(-2N_ue_\pi^2)=\alpha_\pi/(H-1).
\]
Union over the $H-1$ nonreference strata yields the simultaneous
proportion event with probability at least $1-\alpha_\pi$.

Every $D_T$ takes values in $[-1,1]$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:empbern} in both
directions, with range $2$ and $\delta=\alpha_g/(2HJ)$ for each tail,
and take a union bound over the $2HJ$ one-sided statements for the
$J$ nontrivial competitors. This gives
$|\mu_{h,T}-\overline{D}_{h,T}|\le r_{h,T}$ for every $h$ and every
$T\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\{\widehat{S}\}$, except with probability at most
$\alpha_g$; for $T=\widehat{S}$ the inequality is trivial.
Now use \eqref{eq:weight-identity}, bound
$|\pi_h-\widehat{\pi}_h|\le e_\pi$, and insert
\[
 |\mu_{h,T}-\mu_{0,T}|
 \le\min\left\{2,\ |\overline{D}_{h,T}-\overline{D}_{0,T}|+r_{h,T}+r_{0,T}\right\}
 =\rho_{h,T},
\]
where the bound $2$ holds deterministically because
$\mu_{h,T}\in[-1,1]$. Intersection of the two events and a union bound
prove the assertion.
head: environment

label: rem:weight-localization
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:weight-localization}
Because $\rho_{h,T}\le2$, the weight correction never exceeds
$2(H-1)e_\pi$. This crude level holds on the proportion event alone,
does not depend on $|\mathcal{C}|$, and requires no mean intervals: if one sets
$\rho_{h,T}\equiv2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:propweights} holds with probability
at least $1-\alpha_\pi$ and $\alpha_g=0$ may be used in
Theorem~\ref{th:regret}. The empirical refinement through $r_{h,T}$,
in contrast, relies on a flat union bound over the $J$ competitors, so
a factor $\log J$ re-enters the certificate through $t_g$, multiplied
by $e_\pi$. The localization of Theorem~\ref{th:chain} therefore
concerns the audit fluctuation $Z_T$; the weight-estimation term is
controlled only through the factor $e_\pi$, of order $N_u^{-1/2}$,
which is small when the unlabelled sample is large.
head: environment
name: Where the cardinality of $\CC$ re-enters

label: th:regret
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:regret}
Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:unlabelled},~\ref{ass:audit},
and~\ref{ass:pred} hold. Suppose the pilot screening event
\eqref{eq:screen} has probability at least $1-\alpha_s$. Construct
the pre-audit networks as in Definition~\ref{def:network}, use the
observable edge radius from Theorem~\ref{th:empirical}, and form
\eqref{eq:cert-T}--\eqref{eq:regret-cert}. If
\[
 \alpha_s+\alpha_a+\alpha_v+\alpha_\pi+\alpha_g\le\alpha<1,
\]
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:theorem-regret}
 \ \mathbb{P}\{R_B(\widehat{S})\le\overline{R}_{\mathrm{red}}\}\ge1-\alpha.\ 
\end{equation}
If $\mathcal{C}=\{\widehat{S}\}$, define $\overline{R}_{\mathrm{red}}=0$; the
statement remains valid. The distribution $P$ and the proportions
$\pi_h$ need not be known or parametrically specified.
head: environment
name: Honest postselection regret certificate

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{th:empirical} and Lemma~\ref{lem:propweights},
with probability at least
$1-\alpha_a-\alpha_v-\alpha_\pi-\alpha_g$,
we have for every $T\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\{\widehat{S}\}$,
\[
 \Delta_T=\widehat{\Delta}_T+Z_T+
              \sum_h(\pi_h-\widehat{\pi}_h)\mu_{h,T}
 \le U_T,
\]
while $\Delta_{\widehat{S}}=0=U_{\widehat{S}}$ holds deterministically.
This simultaneous event is valid even though $\widehat{S},\mathcal{C}$ and the
network were learned from the pilot, since the relevant concentration
statements hold conditionally on the pre-audit information and counts.
On the screening event, some population maximizer
$S^\star\in\mathcal{C}$. Consequently,
\[
 R_B(\widehat{S})=F(S^\star)-F(\widehat{S})=\Delta_{S^\star}
 \le U_{S^\star}\le\max_{T\in\mathcal{C}}U_T.
\]
Because $0\le R_B(\widehat{S})\le1$, truncation at $0$ and $1$ is harmless.
The union bound with the screening failure probability proves the result.
If $\mathcal{C}=\{\widehat{S}\}$, the screening event implies that $\widehat{S}$ itself
is optimal, hence its regret is zero; off the screening event no
assertion is made.
head: environment

label: cor:regret-one-stage
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:regret-one-stage}
Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:unlabelled} and~\ref{ass:audit} hold, let
the pilot screening event \eqref{eq:screen} has probability at least
$1-\alpha_s$, and let the pre-audit networks be constructed as in
Definition~\ref{def:network}. For $T\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\{\widehat{S}\}$ put
\[
 U_T^{\mathrm{EB}}=\widehat{\Delta}_T+
    \mathfrak R_{\mathrm{EB}}(T)+
    e_\pi\sum_{h=1}^{H-1}\rho_{h,T},
\]
with $\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{EB}}$ from \eqref{eq:one-stage-radius}, and
set $U_{\widehat{S}}^{\mathrm{EB}}:=0$, which is legitimate because
$\Delta_{\widehat{S}}=0$. Define
$\overline{R}_{\mathrm{EB}}=\min\{1,\max(0,\max_{T\in\mathcal{C}}
U_T^{\mathrm{EB}})\}$, with the same singleton convention as in
Theorem~\ref{th:regret}. If
$\alpha_s+\alpha_a+\alpha_\pi+\alpha_g\le\alpha<1$, then
\[
 \mathbb{P}\{R_B(\widehat{S})\le\overline{R}_{\mathrm{EB}}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
No assumption on pre-audit residual predictors is needed.
head: environment
name: Postselection certification without variance calibration

title: Proof
body_md:
Intersect the simultaneous event of
Theorem~\ref{th:direct-empirical} with the proportion and mean
calibration events of Lemma~\ref{lem:propweights}, which uses only
Assumptions~\ref{ass:unlabelled} and~\ref{ass:audit}, and with the
screening event. On this intersection, identity~\eqref{eq:weight-identity}
gives $\Delta_T\le U_T^{\mathrm{EB}}$ for every $T\in\mathcal{C}$; then argue
over a screened population optimum exactly as in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{th:regret}. The total failure probability is bounded by
$\alpha_s+\alpha_a+\alpha_\pi+\alpha_g$.
head: environment

label: cor:representation
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:representation}
Suppose the original corpus contains a larger finite feasible family
$\mathcal{H}_B^{\mathrm{full}}\supseteq\mathcal{H}_B$ with optimal expected coverage
$V_B^{\mathrm{full}}=\max_{S\in\mathcal{H}_B^{\mathrm{full}}}F(S)$.
If, with probability at least $1-\alpha_{\mathrm{rep}}$,
\[
 0\le V_B^{\mathrm{full}}-\max_{S\in\mathcal{H}_B}F(S)
       \le\overline{\rho}_{\mathrm{rep}},
\]
then
\[
 \mathbb{P}\left\{V_B^{\mathrm{full}}-F(\widehat{S})
 \le\overline{\rho}_{\mathrm{rep}}+\overline{R}_{\mathrm{red}}\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha-\alpha_{\mathrm{rep}}.
\]
head: environment
name: Reduced universe versus original corpus

title: Proof
body_md:
Decompose
$V_B^{\mathrm{full}}-F(\widehat{S})
=[V_B^{\mathrm{full}}-\max_{S\in\mathcal{H}_B}F(S)]+R_B(\widehat{S})$
and intersect the two coverage events.
head: environment

label: cor:noise
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:noise}
Suppose the audit measures functions $\widetilde r_j:\mathcal{Q}\to[0,1]$
satisfying the deterministic uniform calibration condition
$\sup_{q,j}|\widetilde r_j(q)-r_j(q)|\le\eta$, and all hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{th:regret} hold for the induced measured coverages
$\widetilde h_S$ on the same pre-audit family $\mathcal{C}$. Let
$\widetilde U_T$ be their simultaneous contrast bounds and assume the
true-population screening event \eqref{eq:screen} has probability at
least $1-\alpha_s$ (Remark~\ref{rem:noisy-screening} gives a sufficient
rule). Then the \emph{true} reduced
regret is bounded by
\[
 R_B(\widehat{S})\le\min\{1,\max(0,\max_{T\in\mathcal{C}}\widetilde U_T+2\eta)\}
\]
with the same joint confidence level as in Theorem~\ref{th:regret}.
head: environment
name: Uniformly bounded relevance errors

title: Proof
body_md:
The map $(x_j)_{j\in S}\mapsto\max_{j\in S}x_j$ is 1-Lipschitz
under the supremum norm. Thus
$|h_S(q)-\widetilde h_S(q)|\le\eta$ for every $S$ and $q$,
so $|\Delta_T-\widetilde\Delta_T|\le2\eta$ for all $T$.
On the simultaneous measured-contrast event and the true screening event,
$R_B(\widehat{S})=\Delta_{S^\star}\le\widetilde U_{S^\star}+2\eta$.
Truncation to $[0,1]$ completes the proof.
head: environment

label: rem:noisy-screening
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:noisy-screening}
Corollary~\ref{cor:noise} requires the screening event for the
\emph{true} population. If the pilot of Proposition~\ref{prop:screen} is
itself labeled with the measured functions $\widetilde r_j$, its uniform
Hoeffding event controls $|\widehat{F}_0(S)-\widetilde F(S)|$, where
$\widetilde F(S)=\mathbb{E}_P\widetilde h_S(Q)$ and
$|\widetilde F(S)-F(S)|\le\eta$. On that event,
$\widehat{F}_0(S^\star)-\widehat{F}_0(\widehat{S})+2r_0\ge F(S^\star)-F(\widehat{S})-2\eta
\ge-2\eta$. Hence the rule \eqref{eq:pilot-screen} must be widened to
$\widehat{F}_0(T)-\widehat{F}_0(\widehat{S})+2r_0+2\eta\ge0$; with this change the
true-population screening event again has probability at least
$1-\alpha_s$.
head: environment
name: Screening with measured pilot labels

label: prop:pooled-bennett
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pooled-bennett}
Assume the model of Section~\ref{sec:model} and let every
$\lambda_T>0$ be fixed conditionally on the pre-audit information and
the audit stratum counts, \emph{without using audit relevance values}.
Then, with probability at least $1-\alpha_B-\alpha_v'$,
simultaneously for all $T\in\mathcal{C}\setminus\{\widehat{S}\}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bennett-pooled}
 Z_T\le\mathcal B_T
 :=\frac{\log(J/\alpha_B)+\mathcal K_T^+(\lambda_T)}{\lambda_T}.
\end{equation}
Combining this with Lemma~\ref{lem:propweights} and pilot screening
provides an alternative population-regret certificate
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bennett-regret}
 \overline{R}_{\mathrm{Ben}}=\min\left\{1,\max\left\{0,\max_{T\in\mathcal{C}}
 \left[\widehat{\Delta}_T+\mathcal B_T
 +e_\pi\sum_{h=1}^{H-1}\rho_{h,T}\right]\right\}\right\},
\end{equation}
with coverage at least
$1-\alpha_s-\alpha_B-\alpha_v'-\alpha_\pi-\alpha_g$.
The bracket for $T=\widehat{S}$ is replaced by $0$, which is legitimate
because $\Delta_{\widehat{S}}=0$; if $J=0$, the certificate
is zero on the screening event.
head: environment
name: Pooled Bennett bound with certified residual moments

title: Proof
body_md:
Condition on the pilot, the independent unlabelled sample and the
stratum counts. For each $T$, define the centered summands
\[
 Y_{h,i,T}=\frac{w_h}{n_h}
   \big(\mu_{h,T}-D_T(Q_{h,i})\big).
\]
Their sum equals $Z_T$, their variances are
$(w_h/n_h)^2\sigma^2_{h,T}$, and, since $\mu_{h,T}-D_T\le2$, they are
almost surely at most $\beta_h$.
Bennett's moment-generating-function bound
\citep[Theorem~2.9]{BoucheronLugosiMassart13}, applied with $n=1$ to a
single centered random variable $Y\le\beta$ (so that $\mathbb{E} Y^2$ is its
variance $v$), gives
\[
 \log\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda Y}
 \le\frac{v}{\beta^2}(e^{\lambda\beta}-1-\lambda\beta)
 \quad(\beta>0,\ \lambda>0).
\]
Summing conditional cumulant bounds across the independent queries,
we obtain
\[
 \log\mathbb{E}[e^{\lambda Z_T}\mid\text{pre-audit information, counts}]
 \le\sum_h\frac{n_h\sigma^2_{h,T}}4
       (e^{\lambda \beta_h}-1-\lambda \beta_h).
\]
When $\beta_h=0$ the variables vanish, so their contribution is zero.
Applying Markov's inequality with the fixed $\lambda_T$ to the event
\[
 Z_T>\frac{\log(J/\alpha_B)+
  \sum_h\frac{n_h\sigma^2_{h,T}}4
              (e^{\lambda_T \beta_h}-1-\lambda_T \beta_h)}{\lambda_T}.
\]
The conditional probability is at most $\alpha_B/J$.
A union bound over the $J$ nontrivial competitors yields an event of
probability at least $1-\alpha_B$ on which all those inequalities hold.
Intersect this event with the simultaneous residual-moment event of
probability at least $1-\alpha_v'$, and replace
$\sigma^2_{h,T}$ by $v^+_{h,T}$ using the monotonicity of the
exponential cumulant for $\lambda_T>0$. This gives
\eqref{eq:bennett-pooled}. The decomposition
\eqref{eq:weight-identity}, Lemma~\ref{lem:propweights}, and the
screening argument used in Theorem~\ref{th:regret} complete the proof
of \eqref{eq:bennett-regret} and its stated coverage probability.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Optimizing $\lambda_T$ \emph{after} seeing the audit labels is not
justified by Proposition~\ref{prop:pooled-bennett}: a fixed-$\lambda$
Markov inequality is not automatically uniform in $\lambda$.
A grid with an explicitly allocated union bound or a time-uniform
mixture construction would be needed for such an optimization.
The same caution applies to choosing a multiscale network on the
audit labels without additional sample splitting or a uniform
complexity argument.
head: environment
name: Data-dependent exponential tilting

label: lem:activity
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Single-fragment swap and activity

title: Proof
body_md:
For every $a\ge0$, the scalar map $u\mapsto\max(a,u)$ is
$1$-Lipschitz. Therefore
\[
 |h_S(q)-h_T(q)|
 =|\max(a_R(q),r_j(q))-\max(a_R(q),r_k(q))|
 \le|r_j(q)-r_k(q)|\le\varepsilon.
\]
When $A_{j,k,R}(q)=0$, both $r_j(q)$ and $r_k(q)$ are at most
$a_R(q)$, and the two coverages are identical. Combining the
observations proves \eqref{eq:activity-bound}. Squaring and taking
conditional expectations gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_h(h_S-h_T)\le\mathbb{E}_h(h_S-h_T)^2
 \le\varepsilon^2\mathbb{E}_h A_{j,k,R}=\varepsilon^2a_h.
\]
The range inequality follows because the difference is in
$[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$. Substitute these bounds into
\eqref{eq:d2}--\eqref{eq:dinfty} to obtain \eqref{eq:activity-d2}.
head: environment

label: prop:rare-obstruction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:rare-obstruction}
For every finite pilot size $n_0\ge1$ and every $\delta\in(0,1)$,
there exist a two-point query distribution and two relevance
functions with values in $[0,1]$ such that, with probability exceeding
$1-\delta$, the pilot observes identical relevance scores for both
fragments on all $n_0$ queries, although
$\sup_q|r_j(q)-r_k(q)|=1$.
Consequently, an empirical supremum of observed relevance
differences, without additional structural assumptions, is not a
valid distribution-free upper confidence bound for the population
uniform envelope.
head: environment
name: Rare-query obstruction to sample-only uniform envelopes

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{Q}=\{0,1\}$ with $P(Q=1)=\theta>0$.
Set $r_j(0)=r_k(0)=0$, $r_j(1)=1$, and $r_k(1)=0$.
The true uniform difference equals $1$. Yet with probability
$(1-\theta)^{n_0}$ the entire iid pilot consists of queries equal
to $0$, on which the scores agree exactly. Choosing
$0<\theta<1-(1-\delta)^{1/n_0}$ makes this probability greater
than $1-\delta$. Thus a pilot-only empirical supremum of zero
is compatible with a population uniform difference of one, and it
covers the true envelope with probability less than $\delta$. More
generally, any procedure whose output on this all-zero pilot sample is
some value $c<1$ covers the true envelope $1$ with probability at most
$1-(1-\theta)^{n_0}<\delta$ under this distribution.
head: environment

label: prop:act-est
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:act-est}
Let $\mathcal W$ be a finite set of pre-audit swap triples
$(j,k,R)$ with known deterministic envelopes $\varepsilon_{j,k,R}$
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:activity}, and let $W=|\mathcal W|\ge1$.
Assume that, for every acquired audit query $Q_{h,i}$ and every
$w=(j,k,R)\in\mathcal W$, the relevance values $r_j(Q_{h,i})$,
$r_k(Q_{h,i})$ and $r_g(Q_{h,i})$, $g\in R$, are observed, so that the
indicators $A_w(Q_{h,i})$ are observed. This does not follow from
Assumption~\ref{ass:audit}, which guarantees only the coverages
$h_T(Q_{h,i})$, $T\in\mathcal{C}$: these determine neither $A_w$ when
$h_S=h_T$, nor any quantity involving fragments outside the retained
competitor family.
For each $h$ and triple $w$, define
$\widehat{a}_{h,w}=n_h^{-1}\sum_i A_w(Q_{h,i})$ and
\[
 a^+_{h,w}=\min\left\{1,\widehat{a}_{h,w}
 +\sqrt{\frac{\log(HW/\alpha_{\mathrm{act}})}{2n_h}}\right\}.
\]
Then with probability at least $1-\alpha_{\mathrm{act}}$, simultaneously
for all $h,w$, $a_{h,w}\le a^+_{h,w}$. In particular,
\[
 \overline{v}_{(S,T)}^{\mathrm{act}}
 =\varepsilon_{j,k,R}^2\sum_h\frac{\widehat{\pi}_h^2}{n_h}a^+_{h,w}
\]
is a simultaneous variance bound for all such swap edges. It can be
combined by taking the minimum with the residual bound
\eqref{eq:observable-edge}, at the additional error cost
$\alpha_{\mathrm{act}}$.
head: environment
name: Simultaneously estimated activity factors

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $h,w$, the random variables $A_w(Q_{h,i})$ are iid Bernoulli
with conditional mean $a_{h,w}$. The one-sided Hoeffding inequality
gives failure probability at most $\alpha_{\mathrm{act}}/(HW)$ for
the displayed upper bound. Union over all $HW$ pairs, followed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:activity}, proves the variance assertion. To take the
minimum with the residual upper bounds, intersect their two
simultaneous validity events and use another union bound.
head: environment

label: prop:swaps
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:swaps}
Suppose two selections $S,T$ can be connected by a finite path
$S=S_0,S_1,\ldots,S_m=T$ in which each consecutive pair differs by a
single fragment swap covered by Lemma~\ref{lem:activity}, with
parameters $\varepsilon_k,a_{h,k}$. Then for each $h$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:multiple-swaps}
 \sqrt{\mathbb{E}[(h_S-h_T)^2\mid X=h]}
 \le\sum_{k=1}^m\varepsilon_k\sqrt{a_{h,k}}.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(h_S-h_T\mid X=h)
 \le\left(\sum_{k=1}^m\varepsilon_k\sqrt{a_{h,k}}\right)^2.
\]
head: environment
name: Pathwise extension to several swaps

title: Proof
body_md:
Pointwise,
\[
 h_S-h_T=\sum_{k=1}^m(h_{S_{k-1}}-h_{S_k}).
\]
Apply Minkowski's inequality in $L_2(P_h)$, then
Lemma~\ref{lem:activity} to each summand. Variance is at most the
uncentered second moment.
head: environment

label: cor:twolevel
title: Corollary
head: environment
name: Two-level improvement over a flat Bernstein union bound

title: Proof
body_md:
For a coarse edge $\widehat{S}\to V_k$, its coverage difference lies
in $[-1,1]$, so its variance is at most $1$ and its range at most $2$
in each stratum. Lemma~\ref{lem:increment} therefore bounds the coarse
fluctuation by $L_n(\log(K_0/\alpha_1))$ simultaneously over the
$K_0$ distinct edges. For a fine edge $V_{c(T)}\to T$,
\eqref{eq:uniform-clusters} implies that the difference is in
$[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$, with variance at most $\varepsilon^2$ and range at most
$2\varepsilon$ in every stratum. Its Bernstein radius is therefore at most
$\varepsilon L_n(\log(J/\alpha_2))$, simultaneously over at most $J$
fine edges (at most $J-K_0$ when the representatives are themselves
nontrivial competitors, since their fine edges are trivial; the
cruder count $J$ is kept for simplicity). The telescoping identity
yields \eqref{eq:two-level-radius}. Because all variance and range
bounds used here are deterministic, no calibration budget $\alpha_v$
is needed. Direct union over the $J$ edges from
$\widehat{S}$ to each candidate yields \eqref{eq:flat-radius}.
Subtracting the two deterministic expressions, and dividing by the
strictly positive term $L_n(\log(J/\alpha_2))$, gives the sufficient
condition \eqref{eq:strict-gain}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Corollary~\ref{cor:twolevel} compares two conservative Bernstein
radii built from variance and range bounds, under common nominal confidence and
the same audit design.
